title: Your Diffusion Model is Secretly a Zero-Shot Classifier
role: Training-free baseline: scores a caption by the noise-prediction error under shared noise, the untrained version of reading score paths for meaning
reads: Squared error ||eps - eps_theta(x_t, c)||^2 at a noised SD latent (64x64x4) of the clean image, text-embedding condition, t uniform on 1 to 1000
trains: Nothing trained by the method; baselines train ResNets on synthetic images or mid-layer U-Net features; one appendix fine-tune on 175 cat images lifts a 2-class pair from 45% to 85%
combines: Class posterior from ELBO differences between conditions, Monte Carlo over (t, eps) with the same (t, eps) set reused for every class (paired difference)
adding: Not addressed for summing conditions; classifier-free guidance combination of conditional and unconditional predictions lowers accuracy, w = 0 best
noise_and_seed: Raw error varies wildly across noise draws while the between-prompt difference is stable; shared (t, eps) and many draws fix it; narrowing the noise distribution fails (Pets 41.3% at eps = 0 vs 87.5% with N(0,I))
timesteps: Single-timestep Pets accuracy peaks at intermediate noise, t about 500 (about 46% of 37 classes, read from figure); uniform timesteps over 1 to 1000 scale best
unseen: no + no held-out concepts; Winoground composition text score 38.5 vs 33.0 OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 (chance 25.0)
headline: Winoground text score 38.5% (chance 25.0%) vs 33.0% for OpenCLIP ViT-H/14, the text encoder SD 2.0 conditions on, Stable Diffusion 2.0
suggests: (inferred) Compare conditions under one shared noise draw, check which sampler steps carry digit identity before stacking steps 0 to 15, and use the ELBO-difference ranking of eps_PoE vs the joint caption as the untrained baseline for 'sum lands on joint'
model: SD 2.0 (zero-shot), DiT-XL/2 (ImageNet); SD 1.1 to 2.1 in an appendix

disagreements.claim: Brief: CLIP's text encoder keeps which word goes with which noun (ratio 0.72 vs 0.13 random)
disagreements.paper_says: CLIP embeddings tend to be a 'bag of concepts' that fail to bind subjects to attributes or verbs; since SD uses the same OpenCLIP text encoder, the Winoground gain is attributed to cross-modal binding.
